This occupation builds and assembles cabinets, display fixtures, and high-grade furniture, or sets up and operates various woodworking machines; it is not an umbrella term for every occupation in the woodworking industry.
Read drawings, study specifications, and plan machining and assembly; measure and mark dimensions on lumber, and inspect dimensions and fit quality, with drawing versions matching.
Select matching lumber by color, grain, material, and knots, and estimate material quantity, type, and cost; do not generalize a single material habit to all products.
Cut, shape, and join lumber and set up saws, planers, mortisers, and shaping equipment; operate only within formal training, equipment scope, and workshop procedures.
Drill, join and assemble, and install hardware such as hinges and handles, using adhesives and connectors; joint quality is not proven by a single dimension problem.

Finish, sand, and protect surfaces, and repair or modify furniture or cabinet bodies, possibly using CAD design or program-controlled machinery; the actual division of work in a position is verified separately.
The U.S. survey covers constant standing, hand use, noise, and contaminants, with protection and accuracy requirements standing out; Chinese shift schedules and environments are verified per factory.

subject.name: Cabinetmakers and bench carpenters
subject.summary: Cabinetmakers and bench carpenters correspond to O*NET51-7011.00, cutting, shaping, and assembling wooden products, making cabinets, display fixtures, and high-grade furniture, or setting up and operating various woodworking machines. The work includes reading drawings, selecting and planning materials, dimension inspection, joining and assembly, hardware installation, and finishing, and materials, processes, and finished-product requirements need to correspond. Site carpenters, furniture finishers, and specialized woodworking machine positions are separated separately; a paper dimension problem does not substitute for equipment training, workshop safety conditions, or actual product inspection.
